meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 13 — Hub densification. Treats Taiwan as a high-centrality node that both influences and is influenced by many external actors. Adds further international deals, dialogues and regulatory frameworks; social-structure consequences of semiconductor concentration (inequality, talent crowding, policy responses); and additional relational nodes that raise the top-level edge density above that of a typical nation.
meta.strategy_note: User insight: Taiwan is a key hub influenced by many and influencing many; social structure is also shaped; therefore many more policies, regulations and deals should appear. This batch raises top-level edge count accordingly.

candidates.title: EU–Taiwan Trade and Investment Dialogue (TID)
candidates.publisher: European Commission / Taiwan authorities (via representative offices)
candidates.description: Regular high-level dialogue on trade, investment, economic security and critical value chains (including semiconductors). The EU is a major source of FDI into Taiwan and an important destination for Taiwanese investment; the Dialogue is the principal institutional channel for managing that relationship in the absence of a formal FTA or BIA.
referenced_by: Broader Taiwan FTA/ECA and dialogue network
candidates.notes: Major non-US, non-China institutional channel. Raises Taiwan’s top-level connectivity by giving the EU a formal recurring node rather than leaving the relationship implicit.

candidates.title: Taiwan–Japan bilateral agreements and cooperation framework (fisheries, investment, customs, patent, etc.)
candidates.publisher: Taiwan and Japan representative offices / related ministries
candidates.description: Dense web of practical agreements covering fisheries, investment protection, customs mutual recognition, patent prosecution highway, product safety, search-and-rescue, environmental cooperation and numerous local-government twinning arrangements. Japan is both a technology partner and a security-adjacent neighbour.
referenced_by: Trade and investment statistics with Japan
New Southbound and broader Indo-Pacific diversification
candidates.notes: High edge-density bilateral relationship that is often under-counted because it is not packaged as a single FTA. Explicitly raises the Japan pole of Taiwan’s external network.

candidates.title: New Southbound Policy — bilateral investment, trade-promotion and sectoral agreements
candidates.publisher: Executive Yuan / Ministry of Economic Affairs / related agencies
candidates.region: Taiwan–Southeast Asia / South Asia / Australia / New Zealand
candidates.description: Growing set of investment-protection agreements, trade-promotion MOUs, and sectoral cooperation instruments (healthcare, agriculture, standards, etc.) concluded with Southbound partners. Complements the earlier New Southbound technology-diplomacy node with concrete legal and promotional instruments.
referenced_by: Outbound investment and trade statistics with ASEAN / India
candidates.notes: Legal-instrument densification of the Southbound diversification arm. Increases the number of discrete external nodes pulling on Taiwan.

candidates.title: Taiwan as high-centrality economic-security hub (meta-node)
candidates.publisher: Derived from trade, investment, semiconductor, defence and dialogue statistics
candidates.description: Meta-node that records Taiwan’s unusually high top-level connectivity: simultaneous deep commercial residual with China, deepening economic-security and technology alignment with the United States, dense practical agreements with Japan and the EU, Southbound diversification instruments, and the global dependence on its advanced semiconductor capacity. Designed so the force layout can assign higher baseline degree / authority than a typical mid-sized economy.
referenced_by: All major bilateral and plurilateral instruments (ART, ECFA, TID, Japan agreements, Southbound instruments)
candidates.notes: Explicit structural claim that Taiwan is not a typical nation-node. Raises expected edge density at the top level of the graph.

candidates.title: Social-structure consequences of semiconductor concentration (inequality, crowding-out, resource allocation)
candidates.publisher: DGBAS / National Development Council / academic and official analyses citing official data
candidates.description: Statistical and policy discussion of how the semiconductor boom concentrates wages, talent, capital, land and energy, producing measurable dualism: high earnings and job vacancies inside the electronics cluster alongside broader youth unemployment, skill mismatch, and crowding-out of non-semiconductor sectors. Official and quasi-official sources increasingly treat this as a structural social issue.
referenced_by: Semiconductor talent pipeline and job-vacancy data
candidates.notes: Direct social-structure edge from the industrial core. Answers the user’s observation that even Taiwan’s social structure is influenced by its hub role.

candidates.title: Labour-shortage and skill-mismatch projections (NDC / Ministry of Labor)
candidates.publisher: National Development Council / Ministry of Labor
candidates.description: Official projections of labour shortages (hundreds of thousands of workers by 2030) and survey data on unfilled vacancies, especially in manufacturing, R&D and technical roles linked to the semiconductor and high-tech sectors. Coexists with elevated youth unemployment — a structural contradiction repeatedly noted in policy analysis.
candidates.notes: Quantitative backbone of the talent constraint and social dualism story.

candidates.title: Family / child policy responses linked to fiscal capacity from high-tech growth
candidates.publisher: Executive Yuan / Ministry of Health and Welfare / National Development Council
candidates.description: Policy instruments (including proposed or expanding child/growth allowances) that are explicitly or implicitly framed as using fiscal space generated by high-tech growth to address ultra-low fertility and family costs. Links the semiconductor fiscal node to the demographic and social-policy clusters.
referenced_by: Fiscal / tax revenue links to semiconductor sector
candidates.notes: Social-policy edge that closes the loop from industrial boom → fiscal capacity → demographic response.

candidates.title: Minilateral economic-security corridors involving Taiwan (e.g. Taiwan–Philippines Economic Corridor alignment with US–Japan–Philippines Luzon corridor)
candidates.publisher: Taiwan and partner governments / related strategy documents
candidates.description: Emerging minilateral arrangements that embed Taiwan’s semiconductor, smart-agriculture and technology investments inside broader US–Japan–partner economic-security corridors. Raises Taiwan’s connectivity beyond pure bilateral deals.
referenced_by: New Southbound Policy and Southbound agreements
candidates.notes: Higher-order external connectivity node. Moves Taiwan from bilateral spokes into minilateral webs.

candidates.title: External regulatory and standards influence arising from Taiwan’s semiconductor position
candidates.publisher: Derived from export-control alignment, industrial standards cooperation, and partner dialogues
candidates.description: The set of export-control, investment-screening, standards and supply-chain-resilience rules that other jurisdictions adopt or coordinate in response to (or in concert with) Taiwan’s central manufacturing role. Taiwan is both a rule-taker (aligning with US controls) and a de-facto rule-shaper because its capacity forces partners to design policy around it.
candidates.notes: Captures the ‘influences many’ side of the user’s hub observation — Taiwan’s position generates regulatory externalities for others.

candidates.title: Taiwan hub → social-structure & policy-response meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from NDC, DGBAS, MOEA, MND and social-policy sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that records the causal chain from Taiwan’s high-centrality semiconductor and economic-security role → concentrated wages, talent, capital and energy → measurable social dualism and crowding-out → policy responses in talent, family, fiscal redistribution and whole-of-society resilience. Makes the social-structure influence explicit for the force layout.
candidates.notes: Closes the loop the user asked for: hub status is not only external; it reshapes internal social structure and therefore generates additional domestic policy nodes and edges.
